1. **Head sensitivity heterogeneity is architecture-dependent and determined by sensitivity *distribution shape*, not GQA ratio alone**: Per-KV-head quantization sensitivity is extremely non-uniform within models, but the *degree* of heterogeneity — measured by Top-5% concentration — varies across architectures independently of GQA ratio. GQA ratio contributes to (but does not determine) heterogeneity; the reliable predictor is Top-5% concentration.

2. **Cardinality constraint is the primary intervention; profiling benefit is architecture-dependent**: On non-consecutive discrete bit-widths {2,4,8,16}, unconstrained allocation — whether by greedy (PPL 32.45) or MCKP (PPL 36.92) — produces catastrophic results because per-head independent profiling distortions compound non-additively when many heads are simultaneously assigned extreme quantization. - **Problem**: KV cache quantization typically applies uniform bit-width across all heads.
